publications.title: CubifyGS: Object-Centric 3D Gaussian Splatting for Lifelong Dynamic Scene Maintenance
publications.authors: Bohan Ren, Dianyi Yang, Shiyang Liu, Yu Gao, Jiadong Tang, Zhilin Lai, Yi Yang*, Mengyin Fu
publications.abstract: CubifyGS is an object-centric mapping framework for lifelong scene maintenance in dynamic environments with frequent rigid object rearrangement. Instead of relying on slow primitive-level re-optimization that often leaves persistent ghosting artifacts, it updates 3D Gaussian assets through spatio-temporal dynamics perception, global asset retrieval, rigid transformation, and explicit pruning. An event-triggered adaptive optimization strategy then refines only the affected regions, improving both artifact suppression and long-term maintenance efficiency on a newly constructed high-fidelity dynamic benchmark.

publications.title: OpenGS-Fusion: Open-Vocabulary Dense Mapping with Hybrid 3D Gaussian Splatting for Refined Object-Level Understanding
publications.authors: Dianyi Yang, Xihan Wang, Yu Gao, Shiyang Liu, Bohan Ren, Yufeng Yue, Yi Yang*
publications.abstract: OpenGS-Fusion is an open-vocabulary dense mapping framework that couples 3D Gaussian Splatting with a TSDF representation for on-the-fly, lossless semantic fusion. It further introduces MLLM-Assisted Adaptive Thresholding to refine 3D object segmentation under open-ended language queries, substantially improving object-level understanding and delivering stronger scene reconstruction and language-guided interaction performance than prior methods.

publications.title: Automated 3D-GS Registration and Fusion Via Skeleton Alignment and Gaussian-Adaptive Features
publications.authors: Shiyang Liu, Dianyi Yang, Yu Gao, Bohan Ren, Yi Yang*, Mengyin Fu
publications.abstract: This work presents an automated framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting sub-map registration and fusion without manual reference-map selection. By combining cross-scene geometric skeleton extraction with ellipsoid-aware convolution and a multi-factor Gaussian fusion strategy, it improves both alignment accuracy and post-fusion rendering quality, delivering more reliable 3D scene representation for robotic perception and autonomous navigation.

publications.title: Transferring Prior Thermal Knowledge for Snowy Urban Scene Semantic Segmentation
publications.authors: Xiaodong Guo, Tong Liu, Yefeng Mou, Siyuan Chai, Bohan Ren, Yijin Wang, Wei Shi, Siyuan Liu, Wujie Zhou
publications.abstract: This work targets RGB-thermal semantic segmentation in snowy urban scenes by addressing both the lack of training data and practical deployment constraints. It introduces the SUS dataset and a knowledge-distillation framework built around MCNet, where prior thermal knowledge from an RGB-T teacher is transferred to an efficient RGB student, leading to stronger segmentation performance than existing methods on both SUS and MFNet.

news.text:
Back in the US after ten years — this time with a paper to present at IROS 2026!
Talk done, poster up. Getting to explain my work and hear what other people thought was easily the best part.
Then came the Pittsburgh side quests: CMU, the National Aviary, and a coffee that somehow tasted like Chinese braised duck. Still processing that last one. Thanks to Lorene for showing us around CMU!
The vlog ended up a little long. Apparently I had a lot I wanted to keep.

A few favorite moments from IROS 2026 and Pittsburgh 🌉
Between the talk and poster session: walks by the river, yellow bridges, a funicular ride, museums, and the Cathedral of Learning. Thanks to Lorene for showing us around CMU! We also made it to the National Aviary and the robotics center.
Walk, eat, repeat. Came with a paper, went home with a full camera roll and a very full stomach. Tired, happy, and already wanting to come back.

news.text:
My first international academic conference: IROS 2025 in Hangzhou! Also my first time presenting at one, so I was pretty nervous 🥺 Still getting used to walking up to people and talking about research.
I also brought an IROS-branded bottle back to the lab. A slightly unusual conference souvenir, but it had to come home with me.

news.text:
Getting ready for A2RL in Abu Dhabi 🏎️
A short look at the FlyEagle team preparing for the autonomous racing competition. Still a little wild to think that no one will be sitting in the driver's seat.

Two weeks at Cambridge on a winter exchange programme, squeezed into a very long vlog 🎒
I filmed the trip on my phone because I wanted something to look back on. Somehow it ended up nearly 38 minutes long.
Thanks to the “Tom Yum” crew for making the trip so much fun.
